optics-report.launch: uniform disk; uniform solid angle inside asin(NA/n)

opsin.referenceMethod: SciPy solve_ivp DOP853; rtol 2e-12; atol 2e-14; max_step 0.5 ms; restart at every pulse edge

physics-report.scope: Numerical verification of these equations and this transport implementation, not independent biological validation or comparison with a different optical transport package.

metrics.convention: First upward −25 mV soma event in [onset, min(onset + 20 ms, next onset)); one-to-one temporal association, not proof of causation. Other events are extra events.

limitations: Published human dendrites and fitted membrane channels; synthetic 60 µm axon stub. No complete human axon or independent optical-response validation.
ChR2 expression density and localization are user assumptions, not measurements from this specimen.
Fixed 34 °C membrane mechanisms; one-photon 470 nm ChR2(H134R) only. No heating, synapses, detector electronics, or trial noise.
The Williams current–voltage fit was characterized primarily at negative holding voltages. Action-potential voltages use its mathematical extrapolation.
diagnostics.eventDefinition: Upward soma crossing of −25 mV, interpolated at integration resolution, with a 2 ms event refractory interval.
diagnostics.outputConvention: States at saved physical times; lightDrive is right-continuous. Pulses split integration timesteps at their exact boundaries. Instantaneous nonlinear photocurrent is evaluated from saved channel state and voltage.
diagnostics.operatorConvention: Native membrane state at t drives backward-Euler voltage at t+dt; opsin and native gates then advance using new voltage. ChR2 current is tangent-linearized at old voltage; its maximum current discrepancy is reported.
